Q: Strategies for bulk-migrating a large Java/JAR codebase and its proprietary dependencies to Node.js/TypeScript A:

Try using AI to read the source code of a Java application and organize all the API interface definitions.

Then, organize the business logic of each API.

Let the AI ​​organize the entire application specification, convert it into a Standard Application Specification (SA) file, and then let the AI ​​generate the corresponding TypeScript code implementation based on the SA file.

Avoid direct one-to-one conversion from Java source code.

For example, if Java uses SLF4J and Logback for logging, you wouldn't want to convert SLF4J and Logback entirely to TypeScript. You should look for a corresponding logging library in TypeScript to replace the Java library implementation.
